concepts.name: battle
concepts.definition: One game between seated players: its table shape is fixed at creation, its armies are frozen copies of saved rosters, and its score, phase, round, missions and casualties are folded from its command log.

concepts.name: command log
concepts.definition: The append-only sequence of commands a battle persists; score, phase, round, missions and casualties are folded from it, undo appends a command rather than deleting one, and a submission names the expectedSeq it extends.

concepts.name: catalogue
concepts.definition: The community rules data rosters are priced and validated against and the public reference is drawn from: BSData definitions, MFM points, Game Datacards rules and missions, and Battlemaster terrain, read only from a verified catalogue snapshot.

concepts.name: catalogue snapshot
concepts.definition: An immutable, checksummed package of every pinned catalogue source with its manifest, provenance and change history; the release pins one in catalogue/lock.json and current.json points at the latest verified one.

concepts.name: correction patch
concepts.definition: An authored source correction in catalogue/patches/, minimal and source-pinned with verified provenance, applied during materialization; a stale one fails the build and leaves the previous output intact.

concepts.name: roster
concepts.definition: A player's saved army list: RosterPick choices for one faction, detachment and battle size that rebuild, price and validate against the current catalogue, with private, unlisted or public visibility.

concepts.name: loadout
concepts.definition: The equipment chosen for a unit's models within the option groups its datasheet offers; choices apply before nested weapon spreads and model allocations.

concepts.name: frozen army
concepts.definition: The copy of a roster attached to a battle: selections, cards, unit keys, model counts and supported wound values frozen on the server after an ownership, price and legality recheck, so later saved-roster edits or deletion cannot rewrite the battle.

concepts.name: league
concepts.definition: An organizer's recurring competition that runs registration, sealed rosters and entrant-started battles as a series of league events; it generates no pairings, schedules or standings.

concepts.name: league event
concepts.definition: One registration cycle of a league: its entrants, assignments, teams and sealed rosters belong to it, at most one is open at a time, and reveal closes it irreversibly.

concepts.name: sealed roster
concepts.definition: A league entrant's roster, repriced, validated and frozen at submission into the league event; saved-roster edits never change it, and only a deliberate replacement before reveal or an organizer unseal after it does.

concepts.name: audience
concepts.definition: Who may watch a player's battles: anyone, friends or nobody. A battle takes the narrowest preference of everyone seated in it; a player with no preference is public.

concepts.name: practice opponent
concepts.definition: A seat backed by an account without credentials, played from a seated player's roster; battles with one are excluded from feeds, standings and service records.

concepts.name: player
concepts.definition: A person using Praetorium through an account: their profile, rosters, seats and record; a practice opponent is a player whose account has no credentials.

concepts.name: account
concepts.definition: The sign-in identity in the account store: user, sign-in methods, sessions and two-factor settings; every player has exactly one.

concepts.name: faction
concepts.definition: A playable army book from the catalogue with its datasheets, detachments and rules; library books that other books import are not factions.

concepts.name: datasheet
concepts.definition: A unit's catalogue record: characteristic profiles, abilities, keywords, composition, wargear options and points, joined from the catalogue's sources.

concepts.name: detachment
concepts.definition: A rule set a roster buys within its faction; each one bought adds its detachment points, enhancements and stratagems, and the roster chooses one force disposition among those they offer.

concepts.name: unit
concepts.definition: One datasheet selection in a roster with its model count, loadout and enhancement; in a battle, a frozen army's unit carries wounds and destruction.

concepts.name: wargear
concepts.definition: The equipment a datasheet offers, priced or free, that a loadout chooses.

concepts.name: enhancement
concepts.definition: A detachment upgrade given to an eligible character unit, priced and limited by the force's construction rules.

concepts.name: stratagem
concepts.definition: A detachment or core rule a side spends command points on during a battle; Praetorium records its use and does not adjudicate its target.

concepts.name: mission pack
concepts.definition: A published set of missions, twists, deployments and terrain layouts from Game Datacards that a battle plays.

concepts.name: force disposition
concepts.definition: The one disposition a roster chooses among those its bought detachments offer; a battle snapshot and an export keep only the chosen one.

concepts.name: side
concepts.definition: One half of a battle's table: one or two seated players sharing turns, command points, victory points, missions and stratagems.

concepts.name: turn
concepts.definition: One side's part of a battle round, folded from the command log; reminders and prompts are scoped to it.

concepts.name: round
concepts.definition: A battle round in which each side takes one turn; round boundaries belong to no phase or turn.

concepts.name: ability
concepts.definition: A named rule on a datasheet, wargear profile or detachment, joined from the catalogue's sources; Praetorium shows its text and models only the effects it supports.
